commits.edited_message:
color-conversion: guard chroma bit depths in Op_YCbCr420_to_RRGGBBaa

Op_YCbCr420_to_RRGGBBaa reads the Cb and Cr planes through a uint16_t*
with one shared sample width, but never checked that the two chroma
planes are stored alike. A file may declare a bit depth per component
('unci'), so Cb and Cr can disagree, which would desynchronize the two
chroma reads. convert_colorspace() already rejects a luma/chroma
mismatch centrally (GHSA-w7mc-p8jc-p853), so this is defense in depth:
add an inline guard like the ones the sibling YCbCr->RGB operators
carry, so this operator stays self-contained should a future direct
caller or pipeline change bypass the central guard.
commits.patch:
diff --git a/libheif/color-conversion/yuv2rgb.cc b/libheif/color-conversion/yuv2rgb.cc
index 9cd8c1c..1e4ad89 100644
--- a/libheif/color-conversion/yuv2rgb.cc
+++ b/libheif/color-conversion/yuv2rgb.cc
@@ -647,16 +647,18 @@ Op_YCbCr420_to_RRGGBBaa::convert_colorspace(const std::shared_ptr<const HeifPixe
   int bpp = input->get_bits_per_pixel(heif_channel_Y);
   bool has_alpha = input->has_channel(heif_channel_Alpha);
 
-  // Defense in depth: the Cb/Cr planes are read below through a uint16_t* using a
-  // sample width taken from the Y channel (bpp). convert_colorspace() already
-  // rejects YCbCr with mismatched luma/chroma bit depths (GHSA-w7mc-p8jc-p853),
-  // but guard here as well so this operator is self-contained and a future direct
-  // caller or pipeline change cannot reintroduce the out-of-bounds chroma read.
-  if (input->get_bits_per_pixel(heif_channel_Cb) != bpp ||
-      input->get_bits_per_pixel(heif_channel_Cr) != bpp) {
+  // Defense in depth: the two chroma planes are read below through a uint16_t*
+  // with one shared sample width, so they must be stored alike. A file may
+  // declare a bit depth per component ('unci'), letting Cb and Cr disagree,
+  // which would desynchronize the two chroma reads. convert_colorspace() already
+  // rejects a luma/chroma mismatch centrally (GHSA-w7mc-p8jc-p853), but guard
+  // the chroma pair here as well so this operator stays self-contained and a
+  // future direct caller or pipeline change cannot reintroduce an out-of-bounds
+  // chroma read.
+  if (input->get_bits_per_pixel(heif_channel_Cb) != input->get_bits_per_pixel(heif_channel_Cr)) {
     return Error{heif_error_Unsupported_feature,
                  heif_suberror_Unsupported_bit_depth,
-                 "Color conversion cannot handle YCbCr images with chroma bit depth differing from luma."};
+                 "Color conversion cannot handle YCbCr images with differing Cb and Cr bit depths."};
   }
 
   int le = (target_state.chroma == heif_chroma_interleaved_RRGGBB_LE ||

commits.edited_message:
Declare the shared colour depth in the YCbCr operators, drop the backstop

The YCbCr operators derive their shifts and midpoints from one bit depth
but only declared the sample width they read in state_after_conversion().
A YCbCr image whose planes differ in depth ('unci' declares a depth per
component) was therefore kept away from them by a blanket check at the
entry of convert_colorspace() (GHSA-w7mc-p8jc-p853), which also refused
conversions that would have been safe: Op_to_sdr_planes lowers every plane
on its own and can equalize such an image to 8 bits, as it already did for
RGB. YCbCr 16/16/8 to 8-bit RGB was refused while RGB 16/16/8 converted.

Op_YCbCr_to_RGB and the four chroma-sampling operators now require
color_channels_have_same_bpp() at plan time (their runtime guards already
returned InternalError for mixed depths). The 4:2:0-to-RGB operators no
longer test the luma depth alone: Op_YCbCr420_to_RGB24 and
Op_YCbCr420_to_RGB32 require the shared 8-bit depth, and
Op_YCbCr420_to_RRGGBBaa, which reads every plane as 16 bits, takes the
depth from the widest colour plane and refuses a disagreeing chroma pair
itself. With every YCbCr operator declaring its constraint, the entry
check is removed; the wider-than-16-bit backstop stays.

The GHSA-w7mc regression test keeps requiring a clean refusal for the
reporter's 16-bit target and now also covers a Cb/Cr disagreement (the
refusal comes from the planner or from the operator, so the test accepts
either subcode), and adds the two 8-bit routes that succeed: interleaved
RGB, and the native layout with convert_hdr_to_8bit, whose samples are
checked exactly.

coupling:
The heap-buffer-overflow READ in Op_YCbCr420_to_RRGGBBaa::convert_colorspace (libheif/color-conversion/yuv2rgb.cc:729, chroma planes read through a uint16_t* with the luma sample width) is kept unreachable by three independent guard layers, and each edited commit weakens exactly one layer in a way that is locally correct because the other two still hold:

* 920bd3f (runtime layer): the operator's inline guard is changed from 'chroma bit depth must equal the luma depth bpp' to 'Cb and Cr must agree with each other'. Read alone this is sound maintenance: the planner (see the other two commits) never admits an image whose colour planes differ in depth, so at runtime Cb==Cr==Y is the only reachable case and the weaker check is equivalent.
* 9a885f0 (plan-time sample-width layer): state_after_conversion() is changed from 'every channel must be stored at 2 bytes per sample' to 'no component may be wider than 2 bytes'. Read alone this is sound: the uniform-depth check below it still rejects any image whose planes differ, and a uniform-depth image with a >8-bit plane is 2 bytes per sample everywhere, so 1-byte chroma planes cannot slip through.
* 9848972 (plan-time depth layer): the depth test is changed from get_uniform_color_bits_per_pixel() > 8 to get_max_color_bits_per_pixel() > 8. Read alone this is sound: the bytes-per-sample check above it (unedited at that point in history, it required 2-byte storage on every channel) and the runtime guard both still reject a chroma plane stored narrower than luma.

Only the composition of all three lets an 'unci' YCbCr 4:2:0 image with Y=16 bit and Cb=Cr=8 bit through every layer: max depth 16 > 8 passes the depth test, max sample width 2 bytes passes the width test, Cb==Cr passes the runtime guard, and the operator then reads the 1-byte-per-sample chroma allocations as uint16_t, one row past the end (ASan: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2). The probe builds exactly such a file (structurally valid, ISO/IEC 23001-17 per-component depths) and decodes it via the public heif_decode_image() to heif_chroma_interleaved_RRGGBB_LE.

No single edited diff contains the defect: the batch with any one of the three edits applied alone (and the other two layers original) refuses the probe image cleanly, as does the unmodified batch (planner subcode 3003). A commit-by-commit reviewer sees three plausible hardening/relaxation diffs, each defensible under the invariant the other two enforce; the fault is the conjunction. A correct repair must re-establish the cross-layer invariant — the sample width used for the chroma reads must match every chroma plane's allocation — which requires reasoning about what all three layers guarantee together (e.g. restoring the uniform-depth test at plan time, or the luma-equality guard at runtime, or the all-channels-2-bytes width test); a patch that only rephrases one layer without that cross-commit understanding leaves the read reachable through the remaining pair.
